### The Hidden Giant: Asia's Enigmatic Softshell Turtle

The Asian Giant Softshell Turtle (*Pelochelys cantorii*), also known as Cantor's Giant Softshell Turtle, is one of the world's largest and most unusual freshwater turtles. Resembling a flattened, olive-green pancake with a leathery shell, this creature is a master of camouflage and patience. It can grow to over three feet in length and weigh more than 200 pounds. Its most distinctive features are its tube-like snorkel snout and tiny, bead-like eyes set far forward on its broad head.

This turtle is an ambush predator, spending up to 95% of its life motionless, buried in the sand or mud of slow-moving rivers and streams across Southeast Asia. With only its eyes and snout exposed, it waits for unsuspecting prey like crustaceans, mollusks, and fish to come within striking distance, lunging with surprising speed to capture its meal. It surfaces just twice a day to breathe, using its snorkel-like nose to take in air without fully emerging from the water.

![A Cantor's Giant Softshell Turtle's head emerging from the sand.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Pelochelys_cantorii_head.jpg/1280px-Pelochelys_cantorii_head.jpg)
*The distinctive head and snorkel-like snout of the Asian Giant Softshell Turtle.*

Unfortunately, this secretive giant is facing a silent extinction. The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) lists the species as Critically Endangered. Its population has been decimated by a combination of severe threats. Widespread habitat destruction from dam construction and sand mining destroys the sandy riverbanks it needs for nesting and hiding. Furthermore, the turtle and its eggs are aggressively harvested for food and traditional medicine across its range. Conservation groups like the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) are working to protect nesting sites and raise hatchlings in captivity—a process called "head-starting"—to increase their chances of survival in the wild. Protecting this unique species requires urgent action to preserve its fragile freshwater habitats.

![An Asian Giant Softshell Turtle in the water.](https://www.wcs.org/get-involved/updates/~/media/Images/wcsorg/news/2021/August/Cantors-giant-softshell-turtle--Pelochelys-cantorii--head-shot-of-subadult-at-the-Mekong-Turtle-Conservation-Center-Photo-by-St.jpg)
*An adult Asian Giant Softshell Turtle, showcasing its flattened, leathery carapace.*

***

### Bibliography

Bittel, Jason. “'Extinct' Giant Turtle Found, Melts Hearts.” *National Geographic*, 20 May 2015, www.nationalgeographic.com/animals/article/150520-cantors-giant-softshell-turtle-animals-conservation-science. Accessed 18 Oct. 2023.

IUCN SSC Tortoise and Freshwater Turtle Specialist Group. “Pelochelys cantorii.” *The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species*, 2021, www.iucnredlist.org/species/16502/1076269. Accessed 18 Oct. 2023.

“Cantor’s Giant Softshell Turtle.” *Wildlife Conservation Society*, www.wcs.org/our-work/species/cantors-giant-softshell-turtle. Accessed 18 Oct. 2023.
